Friends, this is a big milestone for our campaign: **Our first TV ad went on the air across Michigan last week!**
I'm excited for you to watch it:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c6649319-00c7-4df4-96e2-738016c07b9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[WATCH THE AD](https://substack.com/redirect/1467ef74-6ce6-41a8-bca6-7cbaee02155f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We decided to go with this ad because it's about why I love this state. It's personal. It's my story of growing up here in Michigan and what it means to be a part of the middle class. How my parents, who ran a small business, taught me what a hard day's work means and how that drove me to pursue a career in manufacturing.
That's why when I say I'm fighting for Michigan's working families, it's not a talking point written by some out-of-touch, well-paid consultant. That's my life. It's the reason I'm in this fight.
That's the story this ad tells. And for the next two weeks, we need it to be in living rooms all across Michigan - during the news, during the game, in between the shows Michiganders are watching.
**Getting this ad out there matters more right now than it ever has.** The primary is 14 days away, and many Michiganders are voting right now. Fourteen days. That's how long this ad has to reach every voter it can.
I want to pull the curtain back a bit on our campaign strategy and tell you why this TV ad matters so much right now.
You probably know this is now a two-person race, and the polls show I'm the best Democrat to beat MAGA Mike Rogers in November._The Cook Political Report_ - one of the most respected, nonpartisan election forecasters in the country - even said: "If El-Sayed wins the primary, Democrats have little chance of holding the seat."
That's why Gary Peters, the man who's held this seat for 12 years, just endorsed me. Everyone knows Senate control will come down to what happens in Michigan. We can't mess around.
**Let me tell you what TV time actually costs: Running our ad one time during prime time, like during a Tigers game, costs more than $2,000.** It's expensive, but it's a chance for thousands of voters to meet me in their living room. And the data shows TV ads have the potential to really help. That's why we're doing it.
Listen, I don't come from money. I'm not a millionaire. I don't have (or want) a bunch of billionaire backers like Mike Rogers, who had $82.3 million in ad support behind him last cycle.
**But this TV ad exists - my story exists - because this team believed a geeky middle-class kid fueled by a love for Michiganders and a relentless doggedness, belonged in this race.**
I'm asking: if you're able, will you chip in what you can today and help keep this ad on the air through the primary? You'll help us reach folks in every corner of the state these next two weeks.
[CHIP IN](https://substack.com/redirect/c6649319-00c7-4df4-96e2-738016c07b9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you so much.
More soon.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c6649319-00c7-4df4-96e2-738016c07b9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
Trump’s order is the culmination of years of attacks on absentee ballots and vote-by-mail. In the months before the 2020 election, Trump repeatedly spread disinformation and conspiracy theories about the legitimacy of mail-in ballots as he campaigned for reelection. With MAGA angling for total control, Trump wants to end their use forever.
Fuel our work with $35 or more right now to help defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=072126_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Democracy Docket: With New Order, Trump Tries to Kill Off Vote By Mail [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=072126_2&amount=25]
We're going to keep hammering this home, Team, because the mainstream media continues to ignore this executive order and how it will change our elections forever.
President Donald Trump's massive anti-voting executive order has sent lawmakers, election officials, and voting rights advocates into a frenzy. One provision focuses on a goal that for years has been a borderline obsession for MAGA: Cracking down on voting by mail .
For background: After every election in which he's been a candidate or in power, Trump has raged over the use of mail-in ballots in general and ballot deadlines in particular . He's tried to claim fraud for every single ballot counted after Election Day.
So of course, this order directs the Attorney General to “ take all necessary action ” against any states that count absentee or mail-in ballots received after Election Day.
This order makes it clear that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.
We've got to keep fighting and work to protect our elections and our fundamental right to vote. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend vote by mail across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=072126_2&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

We all know that mail-in voting laws are about ballot accessibility, making it easier for voters to participate in our elections . Elderly voters, the disabled, our military service members -- they all vote by mail.
Mail-in voting has happened dating back to the Civil War. It's always been safe and secure , mail-in voting fraud is supremely rare. States have spent millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing. It's been used widely in some states for decades and in most of the country since the pandemic.
Our partners at VoteAmerica said it best: “ There is no good-faith reason to limit vote-by-mail access, reject ballots without postmarks, or refuse to count ballots that arrive after Election Day. If the administration moves forward with these proposals, they will effectively disenfranchise older voters, rural voters, and military voters. ”
Opponents of voting rights have proven they'll go to any length necessary to stop people from voting and make sure that they stay in power. Will you chip in $35 or whatever you can to fight their unending desire for control and protect mail-in voting? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=072126_2&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Mainers have spoken: I am incredibly proud to be their choice for Democratic nominee in our U.S. Senate race.
My name is Troy Jackson. Growing up in Allagash, I didn’t think I’d ever be anything other than a fifth-generation logger. And for a long time, that was more than enough.
But then I got a political education. Not in some Ivy League university — when I was working in the North Woods, grinding out 80-hour workweeks under the thumb of a billionaire. In those woods I discovered the truth: working class people in this country aren’t struggling to get by because we’re not trying hard enough, or not smart enough, or not _anything_ enough. **We’re getting crushed by a rigged system, and we have been for way too long.**
I got into politics after a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages.
I stayed because once I was there, it was clear that _nobody_ in power understood the actual hardships I’d been living my whole life. Working class people deserve to have someone who lives these struggles in rooms where decisions are being made.
Since then I’ve fought to lower the cost of prescription drugs, pass universal school meals, expand rural healthcare, protect abortion rights, and deliver tax relief. And we’ve won a lot of those fights. But there’s always been someone with more power stepping in to water down or block our progress, or dictate just how far we could go. _That’s what happens when our politicians can be bought by corporations and billionaires._
_So now it’s time to take this fight to Washington._
**Susan Collins is the most vulnerable GOP senator — and for good reason. Her voting record is a disaster. Mainers just can’t trust her to look out for our best interests.**
[**I’m ready to win this, but I’m gonna need you by my side. Peter, we’ll start with the bad news.
Not only has President Trump never lost in North Carolina, but this state also hasn’t elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008 – nearly two decades. The odds are stacked against us.
**However, the tide is turning: The latest polls show Democrat Roy Cooper ahead, and experts say this race is now neck and neck.**
Our progress has the GOP panicking. President Trump is trying to put his thumb on the scale by personally attacking Roy online, and dark-money super PACs are investing nearly $100 million so far to halt our momentum. We need your help to fight back.

---
Friend,
In 250 years of American history, we have never faced a moment quite like this one.
**The Democratic Party is being swallowed whole by an openly socialist, anti-American wing.**
This is not name-calling. Their own platform calls for gutting our military, nationalizing private companies, abolishing cash bail, throwing open the border, and handing voting rights to noncitizens.
Their radicals are beating establishment Democrats in primary after primary. Zohran Mamdani was just the beginning.
_But here is what most Americans still do not understand, and it worries me deeply._
**The Democrats have already rigged the system. And they did it through illegal immigration.**
It works like this. Our Census counts every single resident, citizens and illegal aliens alike, when it hands out House seats and Electoral College votes.
So every illegal alien sitting in a blue state quietly pads that state's power in Washington, D.C.
Elon Musk has been sounding the alarm on this, and he is exactly right. Record illegal immigration has already shifted an estimated 15 to 20 House seats toward the Left.
Now you understand why they fight secure borders and deportations so ferociously.
**That is the entire scheme. Flood the country. Inflate the count. Redraw the maps. Lock in permanent one-party power. **
President Trump fought to base representation on American citizens where it belongs. The courts blocked him at every turn. But the plot is now out in the open for all of us to see.
Which brings me to the SAVE Act, and to my single greatest fear in this fight...
Not enough Americans even know what it is. **One poll found that only 23% could accurately describe it.** That is a catastrophe, because you cannot rally the people to save something they have never had explained to them.
**So let me tell you plainly what this bill does: The SAVE Act bars noncitizens from voting, so that only American citizens ever cast a ballot in an American election. And it requires photo ID to vote.** _**Period.** _
That is the whole fight, in two sentences.
And the American people are with us by margins you almost never see in politics. Nearly 80% want proof of citizenship to register. More than 8 in 10 support voter ID, including most Democrats, most independents, every background and every region. It is 5 to 1.
**Yet every single Democrat is fighting to block it.** _**Every one.** _
I have spent a lifetime in these battles, and I will tell you the hard truth. You never win reform inside Washington, D.C. The lobbyists and the entrenched forces always control the inside game.

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

In two weeks, we have the chance to do something huge: send Cori Bush back
to Congress in MO-01.

Cori was narrowly defeated by Do-Nothing Democrat Wesley Bell in 2024
after AIPAC spent over $12 MILLION against her, and Bell hasn’t forgotten
that the pro-Israel lobby sent him to Congress. That’s why he just voted
against ending unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel. ⤵️

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260721-2-cb.whDjkA&refcode=em20260721-38063&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=38063%2E1203867%2E3rvZJx ]A post on X from Cori Bush reading: 'That's a lot of words to say that
you just voted to hand $3.3 billion of American taxpayer money over to
Trump and Netanyahu's wars. For those counting along at home, that’s $3.3
billion more than Bell brought home for STL through HUD disaster recovery
funding.' It is reposting Wesley Bell's statement on his 'no' vote.

This wasn’t a throwaway vote. For the first time in history, a majority of
Democrats voted for the amendment, something that would have never
happened without the relentless pressure our movement has put on them.

But Bell did what AIPAC was counting on and voted NO, proving his
allegiance to the pro-Israel lobby instead of the people.

Sending Cori back to Washington is about knocking down the barriers — and
corporate-backed politicians like Bell — standing between us and real
policy change.

From ending genocide to passing Medicare for All, we can finally win when
we elect more bold leaders like Cori who can broaden our political
imagination and make the “impossible” possible.

With just two weeks until her primary and AIPAC spending big against her
again, she needs all hands on deck. We’re on board for the final sprint,
and we need you with us, Peter.

Families are fearful of the unaccountable ICE agents continually endangering safety in our communities. **Meanwhile, Trump wants to dredge up conspiracy theories about an election from 6 years ago.** 2020's results have been scrutinized down to a micro level. They have been repeatedly litigated in court. **It was a free and fair election, and any public official denying that basic fact is actively sowing chaos that leads our country down a dark path.** It's no surprise that Trump wants us focused on anything other than his failed, unpopular policies at home and abroad. What we're witnessing is a desperate ploy from a man who's repeatedly failed to bend our country to his will. **No matter what illegal force or abuse of power Trump tries between now and Election Day to subvert democracy,****_we are stronger than him._** **Trump is already doing everything in his power to rig the midterms, and now he's laying the groundwork to invalidate any results that don't go his way. The only election interference taking place is in the White House.** So here's my pledge:
* I will keep fighting to debunk the misinformation Trump's administration is spreading about "voter fraud"
* I will stand in full solidarity with my Democratic colleagues in the battleground states where Trump will try voter suppression tactics
* I will consistently share resources and opportunities with you about the best opportunities for fighting back

body:
JoAnna Mendoza, the retired Marine running for Arizona's Sixth District, released a statement following her primary election win.

| | | | | [|

**July 21, 2026****Contact** : press@joannamendoza.com
---
| | **JoAnna Mendoza is Officially the Democratic Nominee to Fire Juan Ciscomani in November General Election**
_Mendoza wins primary election, charges toward general with $3.1 million warchest_
---
| | | | | | **RED ROCK, AZ –** Today, JoAnna Mendoza, retired Marine Corps Drill Instructor, single mom, and native Arizonan running to represent Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District, released the following statement after winning the 2026 primary election, officially locking in her place as the Democrat who is going to face off against Congressman Juan Ciscomani in November.
“I’m so grateful for Southern Arizona’s support for our campaign as we move onto the general election in November,” **said Mendoza**. “This victory comes with the somber reality of our warriors overseas fighting a war that doesn’t have a clear military strategy and objective. Spineless Members of Congress like Juan Ciscomani continue to vote to drive up the costs of groceries, energy, and gas, put healthcare out of reach, and make our communities less safe. Now more than ever, our families deserve servant leadership in Congress, and I’m honored to be the nominee our district is counting on to address the issues that matter most. We can, we must, and we WILL win. Onward to victory!”
The primary victory comes as Mendoza **again doubled Ciscomani’s fundraising in the second quarter of 2026, raising over $2 million compared to Ciscomani’s $1.1 million**. She is heading into the general election with a **warchest of over $3.1 million** and the **support of over 100,000 individuals** , a major feat for a first time congressional candidate. The campaign also released its first television ads of the summer, “[**Heat**](https://us.list-manage.com/kxi34L_s5Y_?e=fea3203902&c2id=b00e5bb4cdbce8e5db7719846a7b67e1) ” and “[**Never Expires**](https://us.list-manage.com/1DeWdCUtXAi?e=fea3203902&c2id=b00e5bb4cdbce8e5db7719846a7b67e1) ”.
###
---
| | **About JoAnna Mendoza** JoAnna Mendoza is the Democratic candidate for Congress in Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District (AZ-06). A proud mom, retired U.S. Marine Corps Drill Instructor, and native Arizonan raised in AZ-06, she grew up in a farmworker family and joined the military at 17. After 20 years of honorable service and several combat tours to Iraq and Afghanistan, she continued her public service as a school board member, veteran advocate, and congressional staffer. Now she’s running for Congress to lower costs, secure our border, and create economic opportunity for working families across Southern Arizona.

Peter,

I've said it before: you can put lipstick on a hog, but it's still a hog.

And what Washington calls "government spending" is really just a trough where BILLIONS of your tax dollars get slopped up by fraudsters every single year.

Con artists in suits and ties, stealing from you in broad daylight — and Washington just keeps handing them the keys.

I want to put a stop to it. And I know you do too. So respond to my poll right now and tell me how it should be dealt with, because I can’t do this without the support of concerned Americans like yourself. ## Feds Freeze $1B in State Medicaid Payments
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. [announced Tuesday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb0TwTAweGLp4S9eO1pN5JCQYLCCJ3K-vXKlf0O1KVzq6535d5guGGNL1E1eyzec50btGao3KvJILCwbnC9E3bZhwfRdaHn4GAQMXmgPMDkPcZ9U564mA-o6s1EZpqcyou5vFxXuJvRPnoXdaKWlGFIMyvRDG94Ppgj1oQgNIIYw8nwjkSAu4QTvTj8vIlCAXWi6new6p3cjHPb-onJa8dtHeWtsq6z8YTAymtG-5tqNiMB1gBpPQR5YMpmflhx-DqfgHvxe-Y3pU_ifK_TO5ylvmC8bgc0kBOSbH15AS1dyQwdQV67Z3iDHUQTMlriuG-Lul_evAl4WfAAAA___NaINH) that the federal government is freezing more than $1 billion in Medicaid payments to California and Minnesota over suspected fraud. California's share tops $867 million, including [$646 million tied](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O2zAUhE8jdRRISjKlgkUadU6bUngmH-2X8A8kbcU5faBd7Am2nsGH-ebXdb8CeYr3nxBQN5f2iEf12BqWPaAlA2RdQfyHGSKEo6D543bJ5YVxxaTcLZB_71NvtUOUOPaohVomJaZlVf1Di-U2caPmyd7WeRVuBDfyVc0wW6Ocgp70SeNKSsH5IuYBpVjRSHtRdhlXs3YTR0stleF3otge6Pw7vbAMJoXe60druXbjj05undyO4xhc-ntanHknt5w8NTK1k1srz5AZ2ECRZXhWind2kpi4sS9ZluEdMLbKAsWINTVgBjy5VCLBZ90VeFpmUsieIBpkJkWDJda-aJsP8p7qRXUTvwcg_7Gzfevcl5b_AwAA__-s2ZLS) to in-home care, where spending grew at twice the national rate. Minnesota's $200 million spans 14 high-risk programs. Kennedy said the payments will return once both states [document that the claims](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OnDAURp_GdB7BhcGmcJGGbtOmRBf7eri7_kG2Z8nk6aMkyhNs_-nTOefH2_aGHDg9vmMk03zeEl01UGtUtkiOLbLzhegXnZgwXoXsh9-gh1n2SgJsDjm8tqlzxhMBjR2ZQelJDZNeVHcY52lfdrjPflRq0OqOetR7rzQtzloaOjZ_3noFMPS9Hu43gmEhC25WTo-LXcTUk-OWy-09c2oH-fDKn1RuNscumKO1s4rxm4BVwHpd1-3CenB6tJzoJ0ZO_6YC1jMHti8B60EY2mGxkIB1mu-zmpSAtfgP-V7kic9KVf7Xl4U47s9SKVJqMnJKVHNDaTGwzyUxSl_w6QSsXTHuvDgErrMSU_-IyOEvaPtS3U8DvwMAAP__bXiRUA) are legitimate. Investigators used artificial intelligence to flag the spending, including [bills for treatment](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAYBp9GMy38VcCA4BKzufRC6xc-Ru4Q55Ada_bpt2ZfYfOu7qr-c1tuHGJI99-8wxR_LAnXGVEK8rLDBcvB-Qx84sGJ9yvD_vMLCZKNUA3R4jjE1zLUzniA0NcwndKD6gY9qXoz3DGvGpK8871dV0gJsUo_kpq8l7YO5m0TiqgTQndjC-omWHJSOd1PdqoGARfKkdu_R0hlg4-v44nc2mOvo9lKeZxV_6uiuaL5uq62bLBIBfn8_8EZb66iOXEJR-JY0cy5BBuxDOMKdpANC8HNsI59o-WqGq2hmUaluhHtVvZYZ-MeV4gxnFJVg7jvHOJ3v_xo2tPQVwAAAP___FWAVg) of patients who had already died. Gov. Gavin Newsom dismissed the freeze as a "recycled political stunt."
## Court OKs Release of Biden Recordings
A federal appeals court has [rejected former President Biden's bid](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb8GNkf2s8F48NCFLV2iqiMy9iN5icHIuEHp11fkFzrd4UhX957v83B2FGm5froZbZnSsOC-RSwF8zBjIO8oTBnxF1e3uHnP6B_TABxaxjUDGIKj-BpUHeyECChrtEJ3SgvVGV3f7ARCuhYkBt8EHRojJslH2QgDHZpG1GSPNq4BBOedaE4IwqCH0OrQSeNNpTgGKimf7omWcsMpvtIT88mnuY72Vsq6VfKjgr6C3o3-eHCwCvqvSwX9ThkvJeXXgdcVXdyYTz-5sIx39GVjIwVc3sHGmPyDZYzoNmQZfcqBluvGhFRGKQ2qzjasO8VIW6srxa-zo_jeUv4l8GnhLwAA__9GLYT5) to block release of audio recordings and transcripts from his interviews with memoir ghostwriter Mark Zwonitzer. The D.C. Circuit's 2-1 ruling found the public interest in disclosing the redacted material outweighs Biden's privacy claims. # If you ever wanted to defend and save Maryland, now is the time.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/bQAPshUmLqf?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) Dear Dan Cox for Governor, I'm a lifelong Marylander. I was born in the city and spent my early life in Takoma Park. My parents moved us to the country in Frederick County when I was turning five. As the oldest of a big family, I didn't know we grew up somewhat poor because my mom and dad made sure through hard work on the farm and in my father's business and later state-wide education ministry that we had everything a kid could want. We worked hard on our farm raising chickens, beef, and livestock. I helped many a summer milking cows on Maryland dairy farms, in between staying in Baltimore's Monkton with my grandparents for summer trips, enjoying the cold waters of the Gunpowder River and the Rails to Trails, traveling with my grandmother to Baltimore City for her volunteering at the Baltimore Rescue Mission outreach. Traveling with my dad to Annapolis to advocate and testify for education opportunity for all Marylanders.

I worked long summer hours throwing hay at $3/hour, filling all the area farmers' barns and hay mows in sometimes 100F degree plus weather. Then, we would cool off in the summer breeze of the evening with cold sodas and ice creams, and sometimes a swim.

Then there were Oriole's games at the old Memorial Stadium where the comeback of the century arguably occurred. In 1988 they had one of the worst losing streaks of 21 games and last place, only to come back under the WHY NOT? slogan the following year to one of the best seasons and nearly first place.

Because of opportunity here before it was so hard to obtain building permits, my wife and I built two houses. We went to law school where I graduated and began my law firm right here in Maryland. And it is where we have birthed our children and served the people in elected office.

That is the Maryland I know. And it is the Maryland of common sense, hard work and opportunity for all.

We see it under direct attack by Wes Moore who is traveling the nation while leaving us behind. Highest electric bills in the nation. Second worst economy in the nation according to CNBC just this week. Hundreds of millions of your tax money missing in the budget and a budget nearly $4 billion structurally in the red. Schools that do not prioritize teachers and students with some of the worst performance tests in the nation, down from where we used to rank near the top. Silencing Maryland voices with gerrymandering. ***And no Key Bridge.*** There is fading opportunity for our kids and retirees to live, work great jobs, save good money, have great schools and retire here.

But it doesn't have to be bleak. You can choose to help us win. Wes Moore is under water, meaning less than 50% of Marylanders believe he is doing a good job for us. That shows the need and genuine interest in new leadership, now. So now is the time for your help. We need to buy the air time, the billboards, the direct mail, the voter contact and outreach and the get out the voter effort. It is a monumental task but with your help together we can accomplish a sweet victory together.

Thank you for joining the effort with any amount. Maryland's [400 program at $2500](https://us.list-manage.com/F8_KYN7IrQX?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b). Our top tier finance team help at [$1000](https://us.list-manage.com/STaC9pbcLEm?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b). And our [Every Voice Matters at any amount $5, $10, $25, $50, $75, $100, $150, $200, $250, $350](https://us.list-manage.com/EIhkOGlpOg6?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

If [everyone donates](https://us.list-manage.com/AXynA1UPU86?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) who opens this email and gets one family member or friend to also donate, we will raise an immediate powerful amount which I have (in the primary) and will again personally matched with my own funds.

Please help us get our message out. That Maryland is worth saving.

Thank you and God bless. And together let's save the Maryland, beautiful Maryland that we know and cherish.

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Governor Nominee for Maryland

Authority: Dan Cox for Governor; Nick Krop, CPA, Treasurer.

The national media are now racing to figure out who Jackson is and whether he'll offer a similar bonanza for political reporters. So what's in store for readers of the New York and DC press when they get the pleasure of learning about Action Jackson?

#### 5\. The Allagash Recount
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/68437cba-5727-4d6e-b7e6-d21fc09c4df4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
First, let's go back to the spring of 2023, to the town of Allagash -- population roughly 240. That year, Jackson decided he wanted a seat on the Allagash select board.
Now, this was already a little peculiar. At the time, Jackson was the single most powerful legislator in the State of Maine -- the President of the Maine Senate. He was also, as we later confirmed, living full-time down in a condo in Augusta, roughly a five-hour drive from the town whose potholes he suddenly wished to superintend. But for the Jacksons, politics has always been the family business, and no office is too small when there's a family name to plant on it.
In the run-up to the vote, Jackson's lobbyist son, Chace Jackson (we'll hear more about him later), started leaning on the locals. The message to town officials was a shot across the bow: he said he was working with an investigative reporter _and_ the Attorney General to sniff around some "ethics" concerns in little Allagash.
Here's how town clerk Susan McBreairty -- a woman who'd been running Allagash's elections for twelve years -- remembered the pitch: he was "working with the Attorney General's office and an investigative journalist to figure out how much" an unidentified party "may be trying to unduly influence the election."
Big if, true. But it wasn't. The Attorney General's office and the district attorney both confirmed they'd never spoken to any Jackson about ballot tampering in Allagash. Chace later conceded he'd, shall we say, embellished the AG part, and had actually meant his _personal_ attorney. Who among us hasn't confused our personal attorney with the Attorney General when making vague threats about a select board election our dad was running in? An easy mix-up. Happens to the best of us. McBreairty put it more plainly: "I called the Attorney General and they didn't know nothing about it."
Jackson himself followed up with a veiled threat of his own, just so nobody up there mistook the family's seriousness. This is how the Senate President spends his spring: menacing a twelve-year town clerk in a town of 240.
Come Election Day, March 24, the good people of Allagash rendered their verdict: Karie Kelly 78, Troy Jackson 70. An eight-vote loss for the most powerful legislator in the state.
Jackson conceded. And then, a few days later, Jackson _un-conceded_.
The Allagash select board election had been _rigged_ against him, despite the Jackson family putting the local bumpkins on notice that they were ready to bring the hammer down on any election funny business.
He demanded a recount.
Come recount day, April 11 -- Troy was _right!_
The hand recount of the original hand count turned up an error. The corrected tally: Kelly 77, Jackson 71. An error rate of 0.67 percent. He still lost, of course. Six votes instead of eight. But thanks to his strident, unflagging concern for election integrity, the annals of Allagash history now record the _correct_ result. Democracy, as they say, dies in darkness -- and it very nearly perished in the Allagash ballot box until Action Jackson rode in to save it.

#### 4\. The BIW Shakedown
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/09fb9eac-0c1e-4731-95b7-f646f34c1020?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Troy Jackson built a career defending the interests of Maine's small but energetic labor unions, sometimes a little too aggressively. Throughout 2019, while Jackson was a state senator, his financial disclosures showed him on the payroll of a loggers union. That union listed its headquarters at the Lisbon office of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, the union that represents some of the workers at Bath Iron Works (BIW), a subsidiary of defense contractor General Dynamics.
In December 2019, Jackson co-signed a letter, alongside then-House Speaker Sara Gideon (D-Freeport), to BIW brass. The letter concerned a tax break the state legislature had extended for the shipyard in 2018. That tax break was worth $45 million and stretched through 2036, conditioned on BIW keeping some 5,500 workers on the payroll.
Jackson, in the letter, scolded BIW President Dirk Lesko for failing to live up to "their end of the bargain," pointed to the shipyard's recently reported plans to bring in out-of-state contractors, complained about declining average wages, and mused, with all the studied casualness of a cartoon mobster cracking his knuckles, that it would be "unfortunate" if the Legislature were to reconsider the company's tax break.
"We championed this legislation based on the promise of continued good-paying jobs at the BIW shipbuilding facility," Jackson and Gideon [said](https://substack.com/redirect/75f0610a-d217-495e-b42b-1293810e0902?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "It would be unfortunate if the Legislature had to reconsider this special tax credit because of the ever-growing evidence that BIW has not lived up to their end of the bargain."
The thrust of Jackson's threat was that BIW needed to funnel more of its payroll through the same union he was receiving payments from if they wanted to keep the tax credits. Coincidentally, Jackson was on the payroll of a union based in the same building as the IAMAW, a.k.a. the union that would have benefited had the threat succeeded.
Lesko, because he has an IQ above room temperature, immediately realized that the letter amounted to proof that Democratic lawmakers were attempting a naked shakedown. The letter quickly appeared in the Portland Press Herald, but nothing more ever came of it.
Now, in a serious state, this would have prompted a criminal investigation into whether Jackson violated the law. At a minimum, it would have marred his reputation and ended his political career. But we're in Maine. So the Democrat Senate President threatening to withhold millions of dollars in tax breaks from the fourth largest employer was barely a scandal.

#### 3\. The Great Potato Shakedown
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c0e8a733-ca16-4dd0-ae24-143db3814b83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On March 5, 2020, Sue McCrum, the matriarch of one of the oldest and largest potato empires in the state, walked into the Secretary of State's office and filed papers to run for State Senate District 2. She was going after a vulnerable Democratic incumbent, Michael Carpenter. Carpenter, who was Maine's attorney general in the 1990s, was also a Democratic ally of Jackson's.
Less than 24 hours later, McCrum quit. She was out before her paperwork even showed up on the state ethics website. No reason for the about-face was given. No explanation that made any sense to the people who knew her. One day, a serious candidate with a serious name and serious money behind her; the next day, poof.
So what happened? Why did Sue McCrum abandon her plans for the state legislature?
The [answer](https://substack.com/redirect/8f8b1449-a1f6-4e54-a299-fec5cbd82e5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to half a dozen people familiar with the events surrounding her decision, lies in an obscure provision the Legislature enacted on June 19, 2019.
Nine months before McCrum's overnight vanishing act, the Legislature rammed through an emergency bill creating a narrow, custom-fit tax credit for food processing. On paper, it was broad economic development: a 1.8 percent annual break on certain business investments between $35 and $100 million, stretched out over nineteen years. In practice, it was a provision that only applied to Penobscot McCrum's investment in a major new facility in Washburn. For the McCrum family, the tax break was worth somewhere between $11.9 million and $34.2 million.
The sponsor of that multimillion-dollar carve-out was none other than the Senate President from Allagash: Troy Jackson.
According to [people familiar](https://substack.com/redirect/8f8b1449-a1f6-4e54-a299-fec5cbd82e5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the matter, Jackson picked up the phone and called Jay McCrum, Sue's husband and the man who runs the company. And the message, as it was described to me, was not subtle: pull your wife out of this race, or you're going to have an eight-figure problem.
Just as Jackson told BIW "it would be unfortunate" if they didn't reward his employer with more union members, sources say Jackson told McCrum that he would use his legislative power to nix the tax credit if he didn't pull his wife out of the race.
That's according to sources who requested anonymity to speak, not the McCrums.
When contacted about Sue's abrupt withdrawal from the race and Jackson's role in the decision, the McCrums declined to comment on the record.
The McCrums' reluctance to talk on the record may have changed following the sale of Penobscot McCrum to McCain Foods on November 12, 2025. Having sold the family company, the McCrums no longer have a pain point Jackson can squeeze to keep them quiet. In an ominous sign for Jackson, the McCrums appear to be fans of Susan Collins.
According to state and federal campaign finance records, the McCrums donated to Collins in 2002, 2008, 2020, and 2026. Perhaps, in addition to a $200 check, the McCrums will donate an on-the-record comment or a starring role in a 30-second ad...
#### 2\. The Gun Control Flipflop
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a230ec6e-e4d3-4a98-a9a0-985ce896b32c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For two decades, Troy Jackson was the rural Democrat the gun lobby could count on. He earned an A- from the pro-gun Sportsman's Alliance of Maine (SAM) in 2004 and high marks from the NRA in 2008 and 2010. He was [endorsed by the NRA as recently as 2022](https://substack.com/redirect/f35895bd-a9b1-43c9-841b-f4f658c7ca76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and took an award from SAM in 2023. He earned those ratings, too. In 2023, he voted against a 72-hour waiting period, against expanded background checks on private sales, and against a bump stock ban. On guns, his record was about as pro-Second Amendment as a Democrat's gets in Augusta.
Then Chace Jackson, his aforementioned lobbyist son, started cashing those gun control checks.
According to a report from the Bangor Daily News, the Maine Gun Safety Coalition, a 501(c)4 advocacy group funded, in part, by New York billionaire Michael Bloomberg, hired Resurgam Group in Dec. 2023.
[Resurgam Group](https://substack.com/redirect/9579aa10-eac8-449f-a3a7-225419e00a81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is the firm where Chace Jackson is a partner. It was founded by Jackson's former chief of staff, B.J. McCollister, and also employs another ex-Jackson staffer, Max Rush. For the 2024 and 2025 legislative years, Maine Ethics Commission documents show Resurgam Group disclosed more than $50,000 in compensation for lobbying work related to gun control bills, with Chace Jackson described as the lobbyist associate handling the accounts in 2024. The payments started weeks before Jackson would begin his last session of the legislature as Senate President.
Jackson had spent twenty years touting himself as a gritty, pro-gun sportsman from the woods of northern Maine. As recently as 2023, Jackson voted "No" on LD 60, LD 1304, and LD 168 in 2023. Those bills were, respectively, an extended waiting period, an assault weapons ban, and background checks.
But he suddenly flipped his position on guns right after the Resurgam contract. At a Jan. 2024 event held by his then employer, the 501(c)4 group "[Food and Medicine](https://substack.com/redirect/9579aa10-eac8-449f-a3a7-225419e00a81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," Jackson said he would support an assault weapons ban, a "red flag" law, a 72-hour waiting period, and background checks on private firearm transfers -- three of the exact measures he had voted against within the past year.
Jackson's defense was that the Oct. 25, 2023 mass shooting in Lewiston opened his eyes. In other words, Jackson continued to oppose gun control measures after the Las Vegas shooting, the Pulse nightclub shooting, Sandy Hook, and Parkland. And, as is typically the case when Democrats seize on a tragedy to push their gun control agenda, none of the measures that Jackson flipped on would have prevented the Lewiston gunman, Robert Card, Jr., from obtaining firearms.
Jackson would not be the first politician, Democrat or Republican, to shift positions as their eyes turned toward higher office, like a gubernatorial bid or a U.S. Senate seat. The timeline, however, is damning: a billionaire-funded gun control group needed the most important vote in the State House, that group started paying the lobbying firm where the Senate President's son works, and the Senate President reversed a twenty-year position in favor of the group writing the checks. The records don't show Troy Jackson took the money himself. It went to his son's firm. But that structure is precisely what makes questions about the payments unavoidable: it's the arrangement you'd design if you wanted the benefit of a quid pro quo while maintaining plausible deniability.
As the Allagash Election Integrity saga revealed, for the Jacksons, politics is a family business.

#### 1\. The Augusta Fraud
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/382ba191-c5a4-41ff-b104-eca3962610a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2019, Jackson bought a home in Augusta -- more than 200 miles from his district in Allagash. He financed the purchase with an FHA loan, the federal program built for low-income, first-time buyers that comes with a lower interest rate. FHA loans has come with an occupancy clause: you have to make the home your primary residence for at least year. Jackson initialed that page.
Then he told the Maine State Ethics Commission a different story so he could be Senate President. From 2019 to 2021, while Jackson was bound by the occupancy clause in his mortgage, he swore in multiple campaign filings that he lived in Allagash. Those two residency claims cannot both be true.
Under federal law, signing a mortgage document you never intend to honor or violating the agreement amounts to mortgage fraud. On the other hand, if Jackson _did_ fulfill his obligations under the loan agreement, then he would have been ineligible under Maine's state constitution to hold the Allagash seat. A real Aroostook catch-22.
The details of Jackson's penny-penching real estate ploy became public, in part, because he [sued the older couple who sold the Augusta house](https://substack.com/redirect/76431368-03c5-400e-a6f1-9723646c9303?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), alleging the sellers hid problems like smoke damage and bugs. The sellers produced records showing everything had been disclosed. The lawsuit collapsed, but not before discovery surfaced something worse: Jackson had also filed an insurance claim for damage he elsewhere insisted predated his ownership.
Like with his residency, Jackson made two mutually exclusive claims about the damage to the house, with each claim tailored to whatever was financially advantageous for him. In the insurance claim, the damage happened while Jackson owned the house. In the lawsuit, the damaged house was sold to him unethically and without disclosure. Similarly, if the damage happened after he bought the house, his statements in the lawsuit were false. If the damage happened before he owned the house, then his statements to the insurance company were bogus. On the one hand, you have a potential case of perjury, and, on the other hand, you have what would amount to insurance fraud.
When [The Maine Wire](https://substack.com/redirect/b0ab28af-9db2-4354-9a7c-877299457581?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) laid all of this out in 2024, Jackson caught brief media scrutiny and an Ethics complaint. His defense was that he [never read the mortgage he signed](https://substack.com/redirect/775ffa64-d817-4ec1-81c0-9659cb45b9e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and initialed on every page, occupancy clause included. "This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," he told the Portland Press Herald. Note the word _unfortunate_. Nothing is unfortunate if everything was legal and he honored the loan agreement. The only way that comment makes sense is if reading the document would have meant declining the occupancy clause and taking a standard loan at a higher rate. He also [threw his own mortgage broker under the bus](https://substack.com/redirect/82372581-7c22-4d70-9b96-e774656b90a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for supposedly setting him up, which is itself an admission that he made an unwise decision to sign a binding financial instrument. The broker denied Jackson's allegations.
Jackson eventually sold the Augusta house for a six-figure capital gain, then kept living in Augusta full-time as a renter. Translation: he used a first-time, low-income homebuyer program to flip a house for profit.
All of this is a matter of public record that any reporter -- or prosecutor -- can verify.
So why no charges?
The only person who can answer that question is the Biden-era U.S. Attorney and longtime Aroostook County Democrat Darcie McElwee. McElwee was most certainly a fan of enforcing mortgage fraud laws against those who commit FHA loan fraud. The [DOJ nailed Merton Weed, Jr.](https://substack.com/redirect/be4ed54a-6d9d-45a9-826d-95922a9f29c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Norway for FHA fraud -- the same conduct -- just months before the Maine Wire exposed Jackson's financial dealings. She's never explained why Jackson benefitted from her, er, prosecutorial discretion. Gov. Janet Mills later tapped McElwee for a judgeship, so she's probably not coughing up any answers soon. For what it's worth, the statute of limitations has not run out.

This is how the Senate President spends his spring: menacing a twelve-year town clerk in a town of 240. Come Election Day, March 24, the good people of Allagash rendered their verdict: Karie Kelly 78, Troy Jackson 70. An eight-vote loss for the most powerful legislator in the state. Jackson conceded. And then, a few days later, Jackson un-conceded. The BIW Shakedown | | ---|---|--- Troy Jackson built a career defending the interests of Maine's small but energetic labor unions, sometimes a little too aggressively. Throughout 2019, while Jackson was a state senator, his financial disclosures showed him on the payroll of a loggers union. That union listed its headquarters at the Lisbon office of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, the union that represents some of the workers at Bath Iron Works (BIW), a subsidiary of defense contractor General Dynamics. In December 2019, Jackson co-signed a letter, alongside then-House Speaker Sara Gideon (D-Freeport), to BIW brass. The letter concerned a tax break the state legislature had extended for the shipyard in 2018. That tax break was worth $45 million and stretched through 2036, conditioned on BIW keeping some 5,500 workers on the payroll. Jackson, in the letter, scolded BIW President Dirk Lesko for failing to live up to "their end of the bargain," pointed to the shipyard's recently reported plans to bring in out-of-state contractors, complained about declining average wages, and mused, with all the studied casualness of a cartoon mobster cracking his knuckles, that it would be "unfortunate" if the Legislature were to reconsider the company's tax break. "We championed this legislation based on the promise of continued good-paying jobs at the BIW shipbuilding facility," Jackson and Gideon . "It would be unfortunate if the Legislature had to reconsider this special tax credit because of the ever-growing evidence that BIW has not lived up to their end of the bargain." The thrust of Jackson's threat was that BIW needed to funnel more of its payroll through the same union he was receiving payments from if they wanted to keep the tax credits. Coincidentally, Jackson was on the payroll of a union based in the same building as the IAMAW, a.k.a. the union that would have benefited had the threat succeeded. Lesko, because he has an IQ above room temperature, immediately realized that the letter amounted to proof that Democratic lawmakers were attempting a naked shakedown. The letter quickly appeared in the Portland Press Herald, but nothing more ever came of it. Now, in a serious state, this would have prompted a criminal investigation into whether Jackson violated the law. At a minimum, it would have marred his reputation and ended his political career. But we're in Maine. So the Democrat Senate President threatening to withhold millions of dollars in tax breaks from the fourth largest employer was barely a scandal. 3\. The Great Potato Shakedown | | ---|---|--- On March 5, 2020, Sue McCrum, the matriarch of one of the oldest and largest potato empires in the state, walked into the Secretary of State's office and filed papers to run for State Senate District 2. No explanation that made any sense to the people who knew her. One day, a serious candidate with a serious name and serious money behind her; the next day, poof. So what happened? Why did Sue McCrum abandon her plans for the state legislature? The , according to half a dozen people familiar with the events surrounding her decision, lies in an obscure provision the Legislature enacted on June 19, 2019. Nine months before McCrum's overnight vanishing act, the Legislature rammed through an emergency bill creating a narrow, custom-fit tax credit for food processing. On paper, it was broad economic development: a 1.8 percent annual break on certain business investments between $35 and $100 million, stretched out over nineteen years. In practice, it was a provision that only applied to Penobscot McCrum's investment in a major new facility in Washburn. For the McCrum family, the tax break was worth somewhere between $11.9 million and $34.2 million. The sponsor of that multimillion-dollar carve-out was none other than the Senate President from Allagash: Troy Jackson. The Augusta Fraud | | ---|---|--- In 2019, Jackson bought a home in Augusta -- more than 200 miles from his district in Allagash. He financed the purchase with an FHA loan, the federal program built for low-income, first-time buyers that comes with a lower interest rate. FHA loans has come with an occupancy clause: you have to make the home your primary residence for at least year. Jackson initialed that page. Then he told the Maine State Ethics Commission a different story so he could be Senate President. From 2019 to 2021, while Jackson was bound by the occupancy clause in his mortgage, he swore in multiple campaign filings that he lived in Allagash. Those two residency claims cannot both be true. Under federal law, signing a mortgage document you never intend to honor or violating the agreement amounts to mortgage fraud. On the other hand, if Jackson did fulfill his obligations under the loan agreement, then he would have been ineligible under Maine's state constitution to hold the Allagash seat. A real Aroostook catch-22. The details of Jackson's penny-penching real estate ploy became public, in part, because he , alleging the sellers hid problems like smoke damage and bugs. The sellers produced records showing everything had been disclosed. The lawsuit collapsed, but not before discovery surfaced something worse: Jackson had also filed an insurance claim for damage he elsewhere insisted predated his ownership. Like with his residency, Jackson made two mutually exclusive claims about the damage to the house, with each claim tailored to whatever was financially advantageous for him. In the insurance claim, the damage happened while Jackson owned the house. In the lawsuit, the damaged house was sold to him unethically and without disclosure. Similarly, if the damage happened after he bought the house, his statements in the lawsuit were false. If the damage happened before he owned the house, then his statements to the insurance company were bogus. On the one hand, you have a potential case of perjury, and, on the other hand, you have what would amount to insurance fraud.
